newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche confirms $1 bln note deal.
newsitem.headline: Roche confirms $1 bln note deal.

text.p: Roche Holdings, a U.S. Subsidiary of Roche Group, confirmed that it was launching an offering of Liquid Yield Option Notes (LYONs), expected to raise about U.S. $1.0 billion.
Talk of the offer was already widespread in debt markets on Friday.
The issue, with a zero coupon, is expected to have a yield to maturity between 6.0 and 6-3/8 percent.
The issue will be exchangeable into participation certificates (Genussscheine) of Roche Holding Ltd at an expected initial conversion premium of between 30 and 32 percent, Roche said.
Roche said the net proceeds from the issue would be used for general corporate purposes. The issue matures in 2012, and is a private placement under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933.
The securities offered will not be registered under that Act and may not be offered or sold in the U.S. "absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration requirements," Roche said.
Roche said that final terms of the offer would be set in the middle of next week.
